narrative: 向上看会把一具身体变成一座建筑。门框、天花板横梁和下巴的底部都会进入画面。
站在门口的老板、一座雕像、一个威胁：人物占据画面的顶部，我们则处在地面。《公民凯恩》（Citizen Kane）专门搭建了天花板（有时甚至挖出一个坑），让这种向上看的镜头有一个真实存在的“天花板”作为限制。
不要把它和一台保持水平的低位摄影机混淆。榻榻米高度或坐姿高度、且视线水平的摄影机，只是一种高度上的选择，接近坐姿平视（Eye Level），而不是低角度。
小津安二郎（Ozu）电影里的房间机位很低，但并没有把家庭成员拍成高塔。如果你在这种设置上向上倾斜，就改变了整句话的含义。
它不适合用在平等对话的场景中，也不适合真正表现摩天大楼的虫眼视角。适度的向上看是一种带有等级意味的肖像。
极端的向上看则属于虫眼视角（Worm's-Eye View）。
how: 把摄影机降到人物眼睛以下（胸部、腰部，或是地面上挖出的一个坑），并向上倾斜，直到垂直线向画面顶部汇聚。更广的镜头会夸大这种汇聚感；同样高度下使用更长焦的镜头依然是向上看，但拉伸感会更弱。
天花板上的实景光源可以顺理成章地成为主光。保持横滚水平，除非你同时还想加入荷兰角（Dutch Angle）。
提示词：low-angle looking up, converging verticals, ceiling or sky in frame, not camera on the dirt looking straight up.
when: 用于表现权力感、纪念碑感或威慑力：一个应当撑满整个门框的人物。具体场景：从一位坐着的倾听者视角拍摄一个站立的人物，天花板横梁在头顶上方收拢。
不要把它当作每个主角出场的默认海报式镜头。
vs: 平视（Eye Level）始终保持视线水平。虫眼视角（Worm's-Eye View）则是从地面或更低处急剧向上看，直到人物变成一座高塔，垂直线向内收拢。
贴地机位（Ground Level）是一种地面高度的机位，可能是沿着地面平视，而不是向上看。高角度（High Angle）则是相反方向的俯仰角。
后备箱视角（Trunk Shot）是从一个容器内部向上看，这是一个特定的场景位置，而不仅仅是一个倾斜角度。
examples_film: 《公民凯恩》（Citizen Kane）通过降低机位向上拍摄，把天花板和逼近的身体一同带入对峙场景。《历劫佳人》（Touch of Evil）在昆兰（Quinlan）身上使用了同样的语法，让他的体型本身成为画面的主题。
《蝙蝠侠：黑暗骑士》（The Dark Knight）经常对服装和建筑向上取角，让人物本身读起来像一座建筑结构。《东京物语》（Tokyo Story）和《晚春》（Late Spring）则是最常被误认的例子：机位很低、以坐姿为准，但大多保持水平，并不是这种倾斜。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的是虫眼视角（Worm's-Eye View）或普通的贴地靴子镜头（Ground Level）。识别标志：画面里只有鼻孔和天空中的一个消失点，或者只拍到鞋子。
修正方法：机位低于眼睛高度，向上倾斜，眼睛和嘴巴依然清晰可辨，天花板入镜。另一个常被混淆的是小津式机位：高度低，但摄影机保持水平。
如果门框和地面线条依然保持正交（没有汇聚），说明你根本没有向上倾斜。

faq.q: 电影中的低角度是什么？
faq.a: 低角度镜头是从低于视线的位置向上拍摄人物。垂直线汇聚，天花板或天空占据更多画面面积，人物看起来比平视肖像更高大。

faq.q: 低角度与虫眼视角的区别
faq.a: 低角度是一种适度的向上看，依然能作为一张正常的脸来呈现。虫眼视角则是极端的：镜头位于地面或更低处，急剧向上看，垂直线向内收拢，人物如同一座高塔。

faq.q: 什么时候应该使用低角度？
faq.a: 当权力感、纪念碑感或威慑力需要通过画面几何体现出来时使用：一个站立的威胁者俯视坐着的倾听者，或是一个站在门口的人物。不要把它当作默认的“美化”手法。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写低角度的提示词？
faq.a: 可以这样写：Low-angle shot looking up at [Subject], camera below their eyes, converging verticals, ceiling in frame. 并说明这不是虫眼视角，也不是只拍靴子的地面镜头。

narrative: Looking up makes a body into architecture. Door frames, ceiling beams, and the underside of a chin enter the picture.
A boss in a doorway, a statue, a threat: the subject occupies the top of the frame and we occupy the floor. Citizen Kane built ceilings (and sometimes dug a pit) so the look-up had a real lid.
Do not confuse this with a low camera that stays level. A tatami or seated-height camera with a horizontal sightline is a height choice, close to seated Eye Level, not a low angle.
Ozu's rooms sit low without turning the family into towers. If you pitch up on that setup, you have changed the sentence.
It is the wrong tool for a peer conversation and for a true worm's view of a skyscraper. Moderate look-up is a portrait with rank.
how: Drop the camera below the subject's eyes (chest, waist, or a hole in the floor) and tilt up until verticals converge toward the top of the frame. A wider lens exaggerates the convergence; a longer lens from the same height still looks up but with less stretch.
Practicals on the ceiling become motivated keys. Keep roll level unless you are also doing a Dutch Angle.
Prompt: low-angle looking up, converging verticals, ceiling or sky in frame, not camera on the dirt looking straight up.
when: Use it for power, monument, or intimidation: someone who should fill the doorway. Concrete beat: a standing figure shot from a seated listener, ceiling beams closing over the head.
Do not pitch up on every protagonist as a default poster.
vs: Eye Level keeps the sightline horizontal. Worm's-Eye View looks sharply up from ground or below until the subject is a tower and verticals collapse inward.
Ground Level is a floor-height camera; it may look along the dirt instead of up. High Angle is the opposing pitch.
Trunk Shot looks up from inside a container, which is a location, not only a tilt.
examples_film: Citizen Kane puts ceilings and looming bodies into confrontations by looking up from a lowered camera. Touch of Evil uses the same grammar on Quinlan so bulk becomes the image.
The Dark Knight often pitches up on costume and architecture so the figure reads as a structure. Tokyo Story and Late Spring are the usual mix-up: low seated cameras, mostly level, not this tilt.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Worm's-Eye View or a generic Ground Level boot shot. Tell: only nostrils and a vanishing point in the sky, or only shoes.
Fix: below eye height, tilted up, eyes and mouth still readable, ceiling in. The other mix-up is Ozu: low height, level camera.
If doorways and floor lines stay orthogonal, you never pitched up.

faq.q: What is a low angle in film?
faq.a: A low-angle shot looks up at the subject from below eye level. Verticals converge, ceilings or sky gain area, and the figure reads larger than an eye-level portrait.
A low angle is a moderate look-up that still functions as a face. A worm's-eye view is extreme: lens at or below ground, looking sharply up, verticals collapsing inward, the subject as a tower.

faq.q: When should I use a low angle?
faq.a: Use it when power, monument, or intimidation should be in the geometry: a standing threat over a seated listener, a figure in a doorway. Do not use it as default flattery.

faq.q: How do I prompt a low angle for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Low-angle shot looking up at [Subject], camera below their eyes, converging verticals, ceiling in frame. Say it is not a worm's-eye or floor-only boot shot.
